ca_k_untch_rock.blurb: Untch Rock is a compact crag in the San Bernardino Mountains above Green Valley Lake, on the south side of the ridge near Crafts Peak. Most of its 18 routes are traditional lines, with a few sport leads and top-ropes mixed in. Grades run from 5.6 up to 5.11, with a cluster of 5.8s plus a fair number of 5.10s and 5.11s, so newer leaders and stronger climbers both find something. The faces are steep, clean and turned toward the south and southeast, set among pines at high elevation. It sits among the nearer crags to the trailhead, which makes it an easy first stop for the day.

ca_laws_caramba_trail.blurb: Laws Caramba Trail is a remote bouldering stretch strung along a hiking path in the San Jacinto Mountains above Idyllwild, running east from Saddle Junction. Most of the 18 climbs are boulder problems from V0 up to V8, with the bulk between V0 and V4, plus a few trad lines in the 5.10 to 5.12 range. Expect steep jam cracks, faces and splitters, often over flat sandy landings. The boulders are spread out and the upper trail is overgrown after wildfires, so it suits a day of hiking with a few problems along the way rather than a concentrated session. The lower trail is in better shape than the upper stretch.

ca_meadows_boulder.blurb: Meadows Boulder sits in open ground west of Saddle Rocks, in the central bouldering zone of Joshua Tree National Park, close to the Hall of Horrors. All 18 problems are bouldering, spread from V0 to V7, with a middle group at V2 to V4 and a cluster of harder V6 lines. The style is steep and built on rounded jugs, which suits climbers who like to pull hard on big holds rather than balance up delicate slab. The walk from the parking lot is short, following a trail for a few hundred yards and then crossing washes and open ground.

ca_echo_rock_e_face_left.blurb: This is the left-hand portion of the east face of Echo Rock, in the central part of Joshua Tree National Park near Hidden Valley Campground. It holds 18 routes, nearly all traditional, with a few top-ropes and one bolted line. Grades range from 5.5 to 5.12, with a good spread through 5.9, 5.10 and 5.11, so several levels of leader can find a line. The wall faces east and has a reputation as a place to slip away from busier formations nearby. Plan on a walk of roughly 10 to 20 minutes from the car.
ca_echo_rock_e_face_left.parking_note: Leave the car in the large gravel lot just north of Echo Tee.
ca_echo_rock_e_face_left.approach: From the right-hand corner of the lot, beside the outhouse, take the trail and old road that run along the right side of Echo Rock, then turn left at the corner. The first route of this section is just right of TS Special.

ca_near_side.blurb: Near Side is a sport crag on Mount St. Helena, overlooking Napa Valley in the wine country north of the Bay Area. All 18 routes are bolted, with grades from 5.6 up to 5.11 and eight of them at 5.8, so it fits moderate climbers best. Approaches are short, and the crag is known for moderate lines. Most routes face south through west, so the wall catches sun from mid-morning into the afternoon with little shade, and an ocean breeze makes a big difference on warm days.

ca_glory_hole_the.blurb: The Glory Hole is a quartzite crag in the Land of the Lost cluster on Horse Mountain in northwest California, within reach of Arcata and Eureka. Of its 18 routes, most are bolted and a handful are trad. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.13, centred on 5.11 and 5.12, so it leans toward stronger climbers. The wall is taller than most of its neighbours and stays shaded for much of the day, a good pick when summer is hot. From the upper parking it is only a few minutes down switchbacks through mature forest to the base.
